habitat: Behaviour and habitat are described as very similar to Green-winged Pytilia: pairs in thorny thickets, often near water.
summary: A locally common resident. Red forehead, throat, rump and upper tail, an olive-green back and orange-edged wing feathers that show as an orange patch on the folded wing. The underparts are barred green and buff. The bill is shorter than Green-winged Pytilia and mostly brown on the upper mandible. The male’s red mask extends over the lores. The call is a flat seee and a two-note piping whistle. The stub has no Kemp estimate and none was added.

similar.note: Green-winged Pytilia has black-and-white barred underparts and all-green wings. Orange-winged Pytilia has green-and-buff barring and an orange patch on the folded wing.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

calls.description: A single flat seee, and a two-note piping whistle. Grade A call from Manyoni, Tanzania. The filename uses the old name Golden-winged pytilia and says the file was edited. It was not cleaned again.

research.note: The colour line also calls the bill red, while the description says the upper mandible is mostly brown. The bill was stored from the description. The female is not given a separate plumage. The stub has no Kemp block and no estimate, and both were left that way. Status is resident and all twelve months are listed.
